Computation Architecture

How Powerful.jl achieves zero allocation in Newton iterations through workspace design.

The Workspace Hierarchy

Three nested layers with clear responsibilities:

SystemBuffers                    # Coordinates all models
├── ResidualBuffers (PQ)        # Data movement for PQ loads
│   └── Residual kernels         # Pure math
├── ResidualBuffers (PV)        # Data movement for PV generators
│   └── Residual kernels         # Pure math
└── ResidualBuffers (Branch)    # Data movement for branches
    └── Residual kernels         # Pure math

SystemBuffers (Coordination Layer)

Contains:

  • Reference to SystemModel (for accessing parameters)
  • NamedTuple of ResidualBuffers (one per model type)
  • Cached metadata (avoids lookups during iterations)

Job: Loop through models, call each model's residual evaluation

Knows: System structure

Doesn't know: Model-specific calculations

ResidualBuffers (Data Movement Layer)

Contains:

  • Variable value arrays (workspace: theta, v)
  • Residual value arrays (workspace: p, q)
  • Address arrays (map workspace ↔ DAE vectors)
  • Active mask (which instances are in service)
  • Instance count

Job: Gather variables, compute residuals, scatter results

Knows: Gather-compute-scatter pattern

Doesn't know: Mathematical details

Residual Kernels (Computation Layer)

Pure functions:

kernel!(outputs::NamedTuple, params::NamedTuple, vars::NamedTuple, active, AT)

Job: Loop over arrays, compute residuals from parameters and variables

Knows: Physics equations only

Doesn't know: Workspaces, addresses, system structure

The Gather-Compute-Scatter Pattern

Every residual evaluation follows three phases:

Phase 1: Gather

Copy from global DAE vector to workspace:

gather_variables!(ws, y)

# Example: Bus model
ws.var_vals.theta[i] = y[theta_addresses[i]]
ws.var_vals.v[i] = y[v_addresses[i]]

Result: Contiguous arrays ready for SIMD operations

Phase 2: Compute

Kernel operates on workspace arrays:

calc_residuals!(ws, model, external, formulation)

# Example: PQ load
@inbounds @simd for i in eachindex(ws.res_vals.p)
    mask = ws.active_mask[i]
    v2 = ws.var_vals.v[i] * ws.var_vals.v[i]
    p = model.pl[i] + model.ip[i] * ws.var_vals.v[i] + model.yp[i] * v2
    ws.res_vals.p[i] = mask * p
end

Result: Residual values in workspace arrays

Phase 3: Scatter

Copy from workspace to global DAE vector:

scatter_residuals!(ws, g)

# SharedRes(:add) mode - accumulate
g[p_addresses[i]] += ws.res_vals.p[i]

# SharedRes(:set) mode - overwrite
g[q_addresses[i]] = ws.res_vals.v_ctrl[i]

Result: Global residual vector updated

Why NamedTuples?

Problem with Dict{Symbol, Any}:

  • Runtime type checks on every access
  • Dictionary lookups (not compile-time)
  • Allocations for boxed values

Benefits of NamedTuples:

1. Type Stability

ws.var_vals.v  # Compiler knows type at compile time

2. Zero Allocation

# Compiles to direct memory read (like struct field access)
# No dictionary lookup, no boxing

3. Compile-Time Specialization

# Each model gets specialized code path
calc_residuals!(ws::ResidualBuffers{Float64, Vector{Float64}}, pq::StructArray{PQ{Float64}}, ...)
# Compiler generates monomorphized version

Trade-off: Can't add fields dynamically at runtime

Why it works: Workspaces created once at setup with known field names based on formulation.

CPU and GPU Dispatch

Same kernel interface, different implementations:

CPU Kernel

@inline function pq_residual_kernel!(
    outputs::NamedTuple,
    params::NamedTuple,
    vars::NamedTuple,
    active::AbstractVector{Bool},
    ::Type{<:Vector}  # CPU dispatch
)
    @inbounds @simd for i in eachindex(outputs.p)
        mask = active[i]
        v2 = vars.v[i] * vars.v[i]
        p = params.pl[i] + params.ip[i] * vars.v[i] + params.yp[i] * v2
        outputs.p[i] = mask * p
    end
    nothing
end

Key: ::Type{<:Vector} matches CPU arrays, @simd for vectorization

GPU Kernel

# Device function
function pq_cuda_kernel!(p_out, q_out, pl, ql, ip, iq, yp, yq, v, active, n)
    i = threadIdx().x + (blockIdx().x - 1) * blockDim().x
    if i <= n
        mask = active[i] ? one(eltype(p_out)) : zero(eltype(p_out))
        v2 = v[i] * v[i]
        p = pl[i] + ip[i] * v[i] + yp[i] * v2
        @inbounds p_out[i] = mask * p
    end
    return nothing
end

# Launcher
@inline function pq_residual_kernel!(
    outputs::NamedTuple,
    params::NamedTuple,
    vars::NamedTuple,
    active::AbstractVector{Bool},
    ::Type{<:CuArray}  # GPU dispatch
)
    n = length(outputs.p)
    CUDA.@cuda threads=256 blocks=cld(n,256) pq_cuda_kernel!(
        outputs.p, outputs.q, params.pl, params.ql, ..., n
    )
    CUDA.synchronize()
    nothing
end

Key: ::Type{<:CuArray} matches GPU arrays, CUDA thread indexing

Automatic Dispatch

# Create workspace with Vector → calls CPU kernel
ws_cpu = SystemBuffers(Float64, am, sys, formulation)

# Create workspace with CuArray → calls GPU kernel
ws_gpu = SystemBuffers(Float64, am, sys, formulation; array_type=CuArray)

No manual branching. Type system routes to right hardware.

How Workspaces Are Created

During solver setup (setup_powerflow_newton):

1. SystemBuffers Construction

sys_ws = SystemBuffers(Float64, am, sys, formulation)

Steps:

  • Iterate through each model type
  • Query metadata for formulation
  • Create ResidualBuffers for each model
  • Assemble into NamedTuple

2. ResidualBuffers Construction

ws = ResidualBuffers(Float64, metadata, am, model_vec, array_type)

Steps:

  • Allocate arrays for each variable (theta, v)
  • Allocate arrays for each residual (p, q)
  • Extract address vectors from AddressManager
  • Initialize active mask from model status field

3. Type Parameter Propagation

ResidualBuffers{Float64, Vector{Float64}}  # CPU
ResidualBuffers{Float64, CuArray{Float64}} # GPU

Flows through entire hierarchy via type parameters.

4. Metadata Caching

# Cache formulation-specific metadata to avoid repeated queries
sys_ws.metadata_cache  # NamedTuple of model metadata

5. One-Time Allocation Principle

After setup:

  • No more arrays allocated
  • Newton loop operates purely by filling existing buffers
  • All array indexing uses fixed address vectors

Cost: Setup takes tens of ms for large systems

Benefit: Each iteration takes single-digit ms

How sys References Flow Through Workspaces

Reference chain:

ACPowerFlowProblem
  ├── sys::SystemModel         # Reference (not copy)
  └── address_manager

SystemBuffers
  ├── sys::SystemModel         # Reference to prob.sys
  └── buffers::NamedTuple

calc_residuals!
  └── model_vec = sys.models.PQ  # Direct reference to model array

Benefits:

1. Modify System Without Rebuilding Workspace

# Change load value
sys.models.PQ.pl[3] = 0.5  # Immediate effect on next residual eval

# No need to rebuild workspace or notify anyone

2. Parameter Sweeps

ws = setup_powerflow_newton(prob)

for scale in [0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2]
    sys.models.PQ.pl .*= scale
    sol = solve_powerflow_newton!(ws, y0)
    # Workspace reused, sees current parameter values
end

3. Clear Data Flow

User modifies sys.models → Problem holds reference → Workspace holds reference → Kernels read from sys.models

Every component sees current state automatically.

Only captures: AddressManager (lives in problem, fixed once assigned)

Performance Characteristics

Zero Allocation in Iterations

After workspace setup:

  • Newton loop allocates nothing
  • Gather-compute-scatter uses pre-allocated buffers
  • Julia heap profiler: 0 bytes allocated after first iteration

Benefit: No GC pauses during solving

Cache-Friendly Access Patterns

Gather creates contiguous arrays from scattered DAE vectors:

  • Sequential access maximizes cache hits
  • SIMD processes multiple elements per cycle
  • Why StructArray (Struct-of-Arrays) vs Array-of-Structs

Example:

# Good: Contiguous memory
v_values = [v[1], v[2], v[3], ...]  # SIMD-friendly

# Bad: Scattered memory
v_values = [bus[1].v, bus[2].v, bus[3].v, ...]  # Cache misses

Type-Stable Dispatch

Every function call in evaluation path:

  • Type-stable
  • Monomorphized (specialized by compiler)
  • No runtime type checks
  • No dynamic dispatch in hot loop

GPU Parallelism

When using GPU arrays:

  • Gather-compute-scatter parallelizes across thousands of threads
  • Each thread processes one or few instances
  • Massively parallel hardware executes all instances simultaneously
  • Scatter with atomic adds handles shared residuals safely

Performance:

  • 2000-bus system, CPU: < 1 ms per residual evaluation
  • 2000-bus system, GPU: < 100 μs per residual evaluation (after warmup)
  • Jacobian computation dominates per-iteration cost

Extension Points

New Buffer Types

Create custom buffer with required interface:

struct MyBuffer{T, AT} <: AbstractBuffer
    # Your fields
end

# Implement required methods
gather_variables!(buf::MyBuffer, y)
calc_residuals!(buf::MyBuffer, model, external, formulation)
scatter_residuals!(buf::MyBuffer, g)

SystemBuffers doesn't care about internals as long as interface matches.

Custom Gather/Scatter

Default: Generic loops over address arrays

Custom: Exploit structure for specialized patterns

# Optimized for specific address pattern
function gather_variables!(ws::MyBuffers, y::Vector)
    # Custom implementation exploiting known structure
end

As long as API matches, SystemBuffers calls your version.

Alternative Dispatch Strategies

Current: Dispatch on array type (Vector vs CuArray)

Extend: Dispatch on element type, memory layout, hardware

# Specialized for different number types
kernel!(outputs, params, vars, active, ::Type{Vector{Float32}})
kernel!(outputs, params, vars, active, ::Type{Vector{Float64}})
kernel!(outputs, params, vars, active, ::Type{Vector{BigFloat}})

Workspace Reuse Across Solves

# Create workspace once
ws = setup_powerflow_newton(prob)

# Solve multiple times with different initial guesses
sol1 = solve_powerflow_newton!(ws, y0_flat)
sol2 = solve_powerflow_newton!(ws, y0_warm)
sol3 = solve_powerflow_newton!(ws, y0_random)

Amortizes setup cost for repeated similar problems.

Parallel Model Evaluation

Current: Models evaluated sequentially (order specified by evaluation_pass)

Possible: Parallelize within pass using threads or GPU

Requirement: Scatter uses atomic operations for SharedRes(:add) residuals

# Branches contribute to bus power balance (SharedRes(:add))
Threads.@threads for i in eachindex(branches)
    compute_branch_flow(i)
    @atomic g[p_addr[i]] += branch_p[i]  # Atomic for thread safety
end

Architecture Summary

Key principles:

  1. Three-layer separation - Coordination, data movement, computation
  2. NamedTuples for type stability - Zero allocation, compiler specialization
  3. Gather-compute-scatter pattern - Enables SIMD and GPU parallelism
  4. Reference-based system access - Modify parameters without workspace recreation
  5. Type parameters for dispatch - Automatic CPU/GPU selection

Result: Production-grade performance without sacrificing clean abstractions.

Quick Reference

Workspace Creation

# Full setup
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
ws = setup_powerflow_newton(prob)

# GPU
prob_gpu = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection(); array_type=CuArray)
ws_gpu = setup_powerflow_newton(prob_gpu)

Residual Evaluation

# Within Newton iteration
gather_variables!(ws, y)
calc_residuals!(ws, model, external, formulation)
scatter_residuals!(ws, g)

Parameter Modification

# Modify system (workspace sees change automatically)
sys.models.PQ.pl[3] = 0.5

# Solve with modified parameters
sol = solve_powerflow_newton!(ws, y0)
